prompt: In Svelte 5, what is `onclick={save}` on a button?
hint: Compare it with `class` or `href`.

choices.text: A directive that only works on elements, never passed as a prop
choices.why: It is an attribute, so it can be passed, spread or left out like any other.

choices.text: An attribute whose value is a function
choices.why: Right. The browser calls it with the event.

choices.text: Svelte 4 syntax that runes mode still accepts
choices.why: Svelte 4 wrote `on:click`; `onclick` is the Svelte 5 form.

choices.text: A call to `save` made once, when the button is created
choices.why: `save` is given, not called; it runs on each click.

prompt: A button holds a `<span>`. A click lands on the span. In the button's handler, which is `event.currentTarget`?
hint: One is where the event started, the other where the handler is.

choices.text: The span, since that is what was clicked
choices.why: That is `event.target`.

choices.text: The button
choices.why: Right: the element the handler is on.

choices.text: The root of the application, because of delegation
choices.why: Svelte's delegation still hands the handler the element it was set on.

choices.text: `null`, until the event finishes bubbling up to the document root
choices.why: Inside the handler it is set; it is the button.

prompt: Why does a `<button>` with only `onclick` work from the keyboard?
hint: What does the browser fire when Enter is pressed on it?

choices.text: Svelte adds a keydown handler to every element with `onclick`
choices.why: Svelte adds nothing; the browser does it for buttons only.

choices.text: Every element with a click handler can be focused with Tab
choices.why: An `<li>` with `onclick` cannot; that is what the compiler warned about.

choices.text: The browser fires `click` on a focused button for Enter or Space
choices.why: Right, which is why the planner's controls are buttons.

prompt: A parent element has a listener added by hand with `addEventListener` that calls `event.stopPropagation()`. A Svelte button inside it stops responding. Why?
hint: Where do delegated handlers wait?

choices.text: The click stops before the root, where the delegated handler waits
choices.why: Right. Stop propagation in Svelte handlers, which know about delegation.

choices.text: `stopPropagation` also calls `preventDefault` on the event, which cancels the button's click entirely
choices.why: They are separate; a button's click has no default to prevent anyway.

choices.text: Handlers added by hand always run after Svelte's own handlers and then override whatever they did
choices.why: Order is not the issue: the delegated handler never runs at all.

choices.text: The button lost focus
choices.why: Focus has nothing to do with it; a mouse click fails too.

prompt: A list of 300 sessions has a checkbox with `onchange` on each. With delegation, how many listeners for that event does Svelte add?
hint: One place catches them all.

prompt: With `AddSession` as a form, what does Enter in the date field do?
hint: What does Enter in a form field do in any browser?

choices.text: Nothing, until a keydown handler is added
choices.why: The transcript added a session with Enter and no keydown handler.

choices.text: It moves focus to the minutes field
choices.why: That is Tab.

choices.text: Submits the form, so `submit` runs
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: It opens the browser's date picker
choices.why: Enter in a form field submits; the picker is a separate control.

prompt: The button is pressed with no date. Why did `look` show nothing changed?
hint: Did `submit` run?

choices.text: `submit` ran, and the page's `add` refused the session because its date was an empty string
choices.why: Nothing in `onadd` checks dates; the handler never ran.

choices.text: The browser checked `required` and refused to submit, so the handler never ran
choices.why: Right. Its message is drawn by the browser, outside the page.

choices.text: The button is disabled until a date is filled in
choices.why: That was lesson 5's version; `required` replaced it.

prompt: Without `event.preventDefault()`, the session of the 21st still appeared. Why?
hint: Who handled the GET submission?

choices.text: Browsers quietly ignore any form submission whose address is the page they are already showing
choices.why: On a plain HTML page it reloads and the session is lost.

choices.text: Svelte calls `preventDefault` for every `onsubmit`
choices.why: It does not; that is why Svelte 4 had a modifier for it.

choices.text: SvelteKit turned the GET submission into a client-side navigation to the same page, so the state stayed
choices.why: Right, and the lesson says not to rely on it.

choices.text: The form has no `action` attribute, so the browser has no address to send it to and never submits it
choices.why: Without an `action` a form submits to the current address.

prompt: A plain `<button>` inside a `<form>` is a ___ button.
hint: What does pressing it do to the form?

prompt: Which line replaces Svelte 4's `self` modifier?
hint: Only when the element itself was the target.

choices.text: `event.stopPropagation()` at the top of the handler
choices.why: That replaces `stopPropagation`, not `self`.

choices.text: `if (event.target !== event.currentTarget) return;`
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: `onclickself`
choices.why: Only `capture` survived as an attribute suffix.

choices.text: `if (!event.isTrusted) return;`
choices.why: That replaces `trusted`.

prompt: Match each Svelte 4 modifier with its Svelte 5 replacement.
hint: One survived as syntax.

prompt: Why is `capture` the one modifier that survived as syntax?
hint: Could it be written inside the handler?

choices.text: It is the most used of them
choices.why: `preventDefault` is the most used, and it became code.

choices.text: It changes how the listener is registered, which a handler cannot do
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Browsers removed capturing from `addEventListener`
choices.why: They did not; capturing is still part of the DOM.

choices.text: Delegation does not work for any event that bubbles upwards
choices.why: Delegation depends on bubbling; it works for exactly those.

prompt: What does `onclick={once(save)}` do?
hint: Read the helper.

choices.text: Calls `save` once now, while the component is created
choices.why: `once(save)` returns a handler; nothing calls `save` until a click.

choices.text: Removes the button after the first click
choices.why: The button stays; later clicks just do nothing.

choices.text: Runs `save` on the first click and ignores the rest
choices.why: Right, with a flag in a closure.

prompt: Why does the `passive` modifier mostly no longer matter?
hint: What did it tell the browser, and what does the browser now assume?

choices.text: Svelte makes every listener passive
choices.why: It does not; a form's submit handler must be able to `preventDefault`.

choices.text: Scrolling no longer fires any events
choices.why: It does; the browser just no longer waits for those listeners.

choices.text: Browsers already assume it for the touch and wheel listeners where it made a difference
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: `passive` listeners turned out to be slower than ordinary ones, so browsers stopped honouring the flag
choices.why: The point of `passive` was speed: scrolling without waiting.

prompt: `<li onclick={…}>` gives `a11y_click_events_have_key_events`. What is the compiler saying?
hint: Who can use a control with only a click handler?

choices.text: Only a mouse will operate it; use a button
choices.why: Right. A button inside the `<li>` was the fix.

choices.text: List items cannot have any attributes besides `class` and `id`
choices.why: They can; the warning is about who can operate it.

choices.text: The handler should be called `onpress` on non-button elements
choices.why: There is no `onpress` event in the browser.

choices.text: Click events are slow on list items, so keydown should be used instead for speed
choices.why: It is about access, not speed.

prompt: Why does `shortcut` return early when `event.target.closest('input, textarea, select')` is found?
hint: Where do arrow keys belong while you type?

choices.text: Inputs cannot receive keydown events
choices.why: They do; that is exactly why the check is needed.

choices.text: In a field the arrows move the cursor, and a shortcut stealing them is a bug
choices.why: Right: the week stayed when the focus was in Minutes.

choices.text: To stop the week moving twice per key
choices.why: One keydown moves it once either way.

choices.text: `svelte:window` only works when no field is focused
choices.why: It listens on the whole window; the guard is the page's own choice.

prompt: Why are the arrow keys a safer shortcut than the letters `n` and `p`?
hint: Think of dictation, and of WCAG 2.2.

choices.text: Letters cannot be detected in `onkeydown`, only in `oninput`, which a window never receives
choices.why: `event.key` reports letters as well.

choices.text: Screen readers block every arrow key, so a shortcut on them never fires for a student using one
choices.why: They do not block them; the lesson's capture moved the week with one.

choices.text: They are not character keys, so they cannot fire by accident while typing or dictating
choices.why: Right, and single-letter shortcuts have to be switchable under WCAG 2.2.

prompt: The special element that puts attributes such as `onkeydown` on the browser's global object is `<svelte:___>`.
hint: The name of the object it listens on.

prompt: Why does `WeekNav` call `onchange(next)` instead of setting the week itself?
hint: Who owns the week?

choices.text: A child component is not allowed to hold any state of its own
choices.why: Children hold their own state; `AddSession` keeps its fields.

choices.text: The page owns it and decides
choices.why: Right: the callback reports a request.

choices.text: Assigning to a prop throws an error in Svelte 5
choices.why: It does not throw; lesson 5 showed it simply does not travel upwards.

choices.text: Callbacks are faster than assignments to a prop
choices.why: Speed is not the reason.

prompt: Why does `AddSession` call `onadd({ date, minutes })` rather than `onadd(event)`?
hint: What should the parent need to know?

choices.text: Events cannot be passed to functions in Svelte 5
choices.why: They can; handlers receive them.

choices.text: The parent should get what happened, not where the input lives inside the child
choices.why: Right: the form could become a dialog and `add` would not change.

choices.text: An event object is too large to pass between components
choices.why: Size is not the reason.

prompt: How does a component call a callback that a parent may not have passed?
hint: The same operator as `{@render empty?.()}`.

choices.text: `onchange?.(next)`
choices.why: Right: nothing happens when it is missing.

choices.text: `$bindable(onchange)`
choices.why: `$bindable` marks a prop as bindable; it does not make a call optional.

choices.text: `try { onchange(next) } catch {}`, so a missing one throws and is swallowed
choices.why: That also swallows real errors inside the callback.

choices.text: `dispatch('change', next)`
choices.why: That is the deprecated Svelte 4 way.

prompt: `Panel` spreads `{...rest}` onto its `<section>`. A parent writes `<Panel title="x" onkeydown={f}>`. Where does `f` end up?
hint: A handler is an attribute.

choices.text: Nowhere: handlers have to be forwarded one by one
choices.why: That was Svelte 4's `on:keydown`.

choices.text: On the `<h2>`, the first element
choices.why: The spread is on the section.

choices.text: On the section
choices.why: Right: spreading attributes spreads handlers too.

choices.text: On the window, as with `<svelte:window>`
choices.why: Only `<svelte:window>` puts handlers on the window.

prompt: In an effect you need a listener on an element. Why prefer `on(...)` from `svelte/events` over `addEventListener`?
hint: Think back to delegation.

choices.text: `addEventListener` is deprecated in modern browsers
choices.why: It is not deprecated.

choices.text: `on` runs the handler before the page updates, so the effect sees the old layout on every event
choices.why: Timing is not what it changes.

choices.text: It adds the listener as the compiler does, so it plays well with delegated handlers
choices.why: Right, and it returns a function that removes it.

hint: Named `on` and a verb.

hint: The page decides last.
items: The browser checks `required` on the fields
The form's `submit` handler runs and calls `preventDefault`
trap: A submission the browser refused never reaches the handler, so the check comes first.

prompt: Which of these can be operated from the keyboard with no extra code? Choose all that apply.
hint: Which elements does the browser treat as controls?

choices.text: A `<button>` with `onclick`
choices.why: Yes: Enter and Space fire `click`.

choices.text: A checkbox with `bind:checked`
choices.why: Yes: Space toggles it.

choices.text: An `<li>` with `onclick`
choices.why: No: it cannot take focus; the compiler warned.

choices.text: A form's text field, submitted with Enter
choices.why: Yes: Enter submits the form.
